alex_k: Heads-up — seeing a big ECC error surge on eu-west-1 GPU pool starting ~09:12 UTC. Error rate jumped from ~0.2/min to ~12/min. Noticed during nightly training window. Anyone oncall?

oncall-bot: ALERT: gpu-ecc-errors (eu-west-1) firing — 12m spike > alert_threshold. Pager duty: srinivas.

srinivas: I'm on it. Pulling metrics now. Can you paste the prometheus query you used?

alex_k: `sum(rate(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m])) by (gpu_card)` — shows sharp tail on 4 cards in the pool. Also seeing clustered Xid=13 in dmesg.

maya_p: raw dmesg from one affected node: ```[ 6142.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=23452, GPU=0, CE: Multiple correctable ECC errors detected
[ 6143.234567] NVRM: GPU fault detected: reason unknown```

jamie_r: Are these all on the same rack/host-subnet? Could be a PSR/voltage issue hitting multiple cards from one PSU.

alex_k: two hosts share the same PDU rack, yes. One host shows higher PCIe errors too.

ops_lead: Quick triage suggestions: (1) isolate affected hosts (mark unschedulable), (2) apply temporary routing to spare pool, (3) raise hw ticket for the rack. We should avoid mass drains that trigger long reschedules.

srinivas: Agreed. Proposed temporary thresholds: bucketize ECC spikes into three buckets: "transient" <5/min (ignore), "burst" 5-30/min (soft-isolate + host-level sched block), "critical" >30/min (evacuate + reprovision). Thinking we should tune alert to trigger action on bucket >= "burst".

maya_p: For "soft-isolate" we can set node annotation `gpu.health=degraded` and let scheduler avoid new pods, but keep existing ones to drain gracefully over 5m. That reduces churn.

jamie_r: We should also enable fallback-routing at the service layer: route heavy batch jobs to us-west-2 reserve pool when bucket==burst to keep latency SLOs. That buys time for hardware triage.

alex_k: Cost note — routing to reserve pool will increase spend ~23% for the window but avoids SLA breaches. Ops prefers targeted card replacement vs whole-node reprovision.

ops_lead: Agreed on targeted swap where possible. Also add throttled retry in the runtime: increase grpc retry backoff for that pool to reduce load amplification.

srinivas: Doing manual soft-isolation now: `kubectl annotate node gpu-eu-west-1-az3-12 gpu.health=degraded` then `kubectl cordon --overwrite` for new-scheduler rules. Will monitor for 15m.

oncall-bot: NOTE: Route change executed by ops-bot — shifting batch jobs to reserve pool us-west-2.

maya_p: Follow-up checklist for post-triage: capture full dmesg + nvml logs, gather per-card ECC counters from nvml, snapshot scheduler events, vendor ticket # (if created). I can own the logs bundle.

jamie_r: Long-term action: we should implement an automated 'graceful failover' policy: detect rack-correlated ECC patterns and automatically isolate racks (not just nodes) to avoid cascading replacements. Also consider PEM/voltage telemetry ingestion.

alex_k: One more: let's lower the ephemeral 'burst' window to 3m for faster detection but keep action conservative to avoid flapping.

ops_lead: Plan approved. srinivas continue monitoring; maya collect logs; I'll open a vendor ticket and authorize targeted replacements if card-level ECC > 1e5 within 24h. Keep channel updated. :thumbsup:

srinivas: Update — error rate dropped to ~1.1/min after isolating two hosts and routing. Continuing to watch.

alex_k: Thanks all. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and proposed runbook updates (thresholds + rack-isolate automation).
